newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee trade frozen as world prices swing.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee trade frozen as world prices swing.

text.p: Coffee trade in Vietnam slowed almost to a halt this week with farmers and dealers preferring to stay sidelined amid continued volatility on world markets, traders said on Friday.
"There's very little business in either the internal or FOB market. People are scared," said one trader.
On Thursday morning offers were $1,200 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, but by the evening prices had risen to $1,320 in line with increases in London.
A week ago Vietnam robusta was trading at around $1,400 per tonne FOB Saigon port.
"If you're a speculator on world markets it's been perfect. But if you are someone with your hands on the physical product it's really not been good in recent months," said a local merchant.

Predictions varied about likely movements in London later on Friday with some dealers saying prices would drop following late profit-taking in New York, and others saying the market might quiet down ahead of the weekend.
"But volatility is with us to stay," said a regional dealer.
"The Brazilian winter hasn't even started yet June and July are going to be hell. It's a nightmare for everyone. We want volatility, but not this much."
